newsitem.title: GERMANY: UPS German consignments up three pct in 96.
newsitem.headline: UPS German consignments up three pct in 96.

text.p: United Parcel Service of America (UPS) said consignments transported in Germany rose three percent to 124.4 million in 1996.
The global parcels carrier said UPS Standard, its domestic and European service amounting to more than 90 percent of German consignments, showed satisfactory growth.
UPS Express consignments, representing under 10 percent of total business, grew 22.4 percent last year, a company statement said.
Marketing manager Ralf Fege said the growth rates "are a clear sign that our new European service meets the needs of our clients in Germany".
The company had invested in information technology and developed quality, client-orientated products to achieve its aim of becoming express market leader in Germany, he added.

UPS does not publish Germany revenue or profits figures but a survey by the German federal office for post and telecommunications said in March that the parcels company had turnover of 1.19 billion marks in 1995.
A UPS spokesman declined to comment on the figure but noted that UPS achieved "satisfactory results" in Germany.
"We expect small growth rates in express in 1997. We will certainly not have double-figure growth for standard consignments," he said.
UPS had a wide client base and high volume and was seeking in particular to increase its express consignment volumes, he added.
